title: Ford simplifies using your EV as a home battery with the $30K Fathom
gist: Ford's sub-$30,000 Fathom electric pickup, due next year, builds the bidirectional inverter into the truck, cutting the cost of home backup power versus the F-150 Lightning setup, while competing with the bare-bones Blank Slate.

insights.claim: Every Ford Fathom will include an onboard inverter, so it can act as a home backup battery without an inverter-equipped wallbox like the Lightning's 80 A unit.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Bundling the inverter makes V2H standard rather than an upsell, shifting the economics of home storage.

insights.claim: Ford says the new Home Power Station should cost about half the $1,310 older unit and the new Home Backup Panel about 60 percent less than the roughly $5,000 first-generation panel.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Lower V2H hardware costs could improve payback versus stationary batteries.
insights.locator: Paragraphs beginning "Now, the Fathom won't need"

insights.claim: The Fathom is the first sub-$30k bidirectional EV with AC power; software charges when electricity is cheap and powers the house when rates are expensive.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Rate arbitrage use case ties EVs to utility tariffs.

insights.claim: Ford is working with utilities in the US and Canada on vehicle-to-grid pilots and certified the system to UL 1741, IEEE 1547 and SAE J3068.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: V2G pilots could open grid-service revenue for EV owners.

insights.claim: Ford's Fathom costs about $5,000 more than the startup Blank Slate bare-bones truck but adds two doors, infotainment, CarPlay and a dealership service network.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Two opposing strategies for cheap EVs test whether buyers want minimalism or conventional features.

insights.claim: The author says Ford built the Fathom by studying how Chinese EVs reach such low prices, and the charging module is one of five computers that replace dozens of ECUs in a software-defined design.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Legacy automakers are copying Chinese cost structures and architectures.
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning "The other is the result"
